study type: Retrospective cross-sectional study using administrative data
cohort: The study included 6,357,796 childbirth hospitalizations from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project's National Inpatient Sample, comprising 2,932,234 Medicaid-funded and 3,425,562 privately insured births.
finding: The highest rate of SMMM (224.9 per 10,000 births) occurred among rural Indigenous Medicaid-funded births, with elevated rates also found among Black rural and urban residents and Hispanic urban residents with Medicaid funding, indicating significant additive interactions.
mod_finding: 19% of SMMM cases among patients with cesarean birth were attributable to payer interaction.
